answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the atlas check immediately, the jetty audit keeps the resolved set and the inlet replay reveals exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 30 aliases as a result pays the reading cost 30 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
